OPM got hacked; most people don't know what the OPM does or doesn't do, and then the press went nuts over it.

OPM stands for the Office of Personnel Management, they use contractors for quite a bit of their work.

They have contractors do security clearance investigations for some agencies. Intelligence branches within the DoD (army, navy, marines, air force, etc.) generally use their own resources to vet personnel; it is done internally and they don't use the OPM... because of the risk of this kind of shit happening.

I say "generally" because of the requirements these branches have for fields...

Here is an example: A gruntling gets a 'secret' level security clearance, through the OPM. This is the kind of stuff a soldier has access and exposure to.

An intelligence analyst in the army has a TS/SCI clearance, through the army. This is the kind of information that needs to be broken up, and an average soldier never knowingly has access to.

What makes this so ironic, is that the OPM was really concerned about internal security and counterintelligence against internal threats a few years back, right before the Snowden debacle.

Here is an example from 2013, after Snowden

Is the hack bad? Well, yes, because people can be extorted.

But understand that any covert operative wouldn't have their real identity in a computer system in the first place.

These groups use couriers, physical encryption, and steganography; methods that don't rely on electricity, creature comforts, and the like. So, the idea that they'd put an identity on a computer that could be hacked is laughable.

The OPM doesn't even handle TS/SCI (non-covert,) clearances for quite a few agencies; vetting is done in-house.
